newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis sees France, Germany "assuredly" in EMU.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis sees France, Germany "assuredly" in EMU.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Sunday France and Germany would be part of the launch of European monetary union but stopped short of naming any other likely candidates to launch a single currency.
Speaking on RTL radio, he reiterated that France's economic growth forecast of 2.3 percent in 1997 was a minimum and that he hoped the coming months would show growth could be stronger.
He also said he expected unemployment to dip in the second half of the year and that the drop would be compounded in 1998.
Asked who would launch EMU, Arthuis said: "France assuredly, Germany too, and the greatest possible number (of others)."

Asked if Italy would be there to from the outset, Arthuis said: "I have confidence in all the governments which have set themselves the task of taking the necessary steps to get there. We will see the results in spring 1998 when the decisions will be taken."

European Union finance ministers said after a meeting in the Netherlands on Saturday that the decision on who would take part in the January 1, 1999 launch of monetary union would be taken at the end of April or in early May of 1998.

Regarding France's 1998 budget preparations, Arthuis said the matter would be debated in parliament in May but dismissed a suggestion from his interviewers that the government would have to look for budget savings of as high as 80 billion francs.
"We have to find savings," he said. But, on the suggestion that up to 80 billion francs in savings would be needed, he replied: "All this looks excessive to me."

He asknowledged that France's public deficit would have come in at 3.45 percent as a proportion of gross domestic product in 1997 -- the year when deficits are supposed to be limited to 3.0 percent of GDP to qualify for EMU -- if 37.5 billion francs in funds transferred from France Telecom had not been included.
He said the public deficit had been whittled down steadily over the last several years and would continue to be cut. "Three percent is not bad ... but equiibrium is the goal," he said.

On jobs, Arthuis said, "I have good reason to hope for a stabilisation in unemployment in the first half (of this year) and for a fall in unemployment in the second half which should be compounded in 1998."
Arthuis said corporate investment was weak and was a crucial ingredient for underpinning growth.

The government was considering measures to help investment among small and medium sized companies but the government could not be expected to do all the work and big companies with good cash resources should do their bit too, he said.
The government was looking at two ideas regarding small and medium sized companies, one on the tax side, where any incentive measures would be retroactive to January 1997.
Asked about the scale of any government plan to boost small company investment levels, Arthuis said it would be "less than a billion francs."
Another option being considered, he said, was using some of the government's privatisation revenues to provide funds for agencies which subsribed to the shareholder capital of small firms.
"(But) we cant expect the state to do everything ... I want the world of big enterprise mobilising too," he said.
